newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest milling wheat limit-down on Chicago price.
newsitem.headline: Budapest milling wheat limit-down on Chicago price.

text.p: Milling wheat futures prices continued to drop on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Tuesday, mainly led by Chicago's price drop on Monday, traders said.
"Chicago prices continued their downward movement and the Budapest market reflected that," said Istvan Grebats of brokerage Termin.
"There was also a significant selling pressure".

Milling wheat futures dropped the daily allowed 400 forints per tonne for all but the July maturity, which found some support due to position-closing, but it also finished 340 forints lower at 20,410.
Grebats said milling wheat prices would depend to a great extent on the weather during harvesting as rains could lower the quality of some of the wheat to feed grade.
"This could raise the relative value of milling wheat and depress prices of feeds".
He said current milling wheat prices for the more distant maturities were already low enough for buyers to appear, but this had not happened yet.
Maize futures edged 100 to 220 forints lower for October, November and December and only July bucked the trend as it rose 80 forints to 21,080.
Current weather conditions were favourable to maize, Grebats said, but a drought could always change the good crop outlook.
1998 maturities remained flat and were untraded.
Total grains turnover on the BCE was a below-average 1,352 lots or 592.97 million forints, down from Monday's 1,496 lots or 648.93 million forints.
Milling wheat futures accounted for about half the turnover in volume terms with 727 lots.
